data.text/markdown:
Data file format

For each set of 3-regular graphs ||(G_i||) with a given vertex number ||(|V|||) and dual to the 2-sphere ||(S^2||), the descriptions of these graphs are stored in .npz files for later use. This document explains how the files V=vvv-Pachner-graph-base.npz are formatted, where vvv is an even number giving ||(|V|||). The files contain the following:
  • edge_lists
  • group_elements, group_ptr
  • matrix_col, matrix_data, matrix_indptr
  • move_edges, move_perms
The details of these various entries are provided below.

Graph information

The first few entries give the data necessary to reconstruct the graphs themselves, as well as their symmetry groups. edge_lists: An np.array of size (N_graph, N_edge, 2), where N_graph is the number of non-isomorphic graphs with ||(|V|||) vertices, N_edges = ||(3|V| / 2||) is the number of edges for all these graphs, and each edge is of the form (start, end) for the two incident vertex labels, with start < end. Thus, edge_lists[iii] is the list of edges for graph iii in the canonical list. The entries are in np.uint8 format, which is sufficient for ||(|V| <= 255||). The edges are given in implicit order, meaning the edges appear in the same order as they do in the cyclic order around each vertex, in CCW arrangement. group_elements, group_ptr: These two arrays provide all information to reconstruct the automorphism group of the graph structures. The group elements are given as a list of permutations of the edges; thus, each element is an np.array of shape (N_edges) of signed edge indices. A negative edge label records a flip in the orientation of the edge under the group element. Recall that the number of edges ||(|E|||) (or N_edges) in a graph is ||(|E| = 3|V| / 2||). In general, the groups will be of arbitrary size, so this information is recorded in group_ptr, which is an np.array recording where each group starts and stops in group_elements. Specifically, if we want the symmetry group for graph iii, then they are the elements in the list group_elements[group_ptr[iii], group_ptr[iii + 1]]. This means that group_ptr is an array of length (N_graph + 1) with np.uint16 entries, and group_elements is an np.array of shape (N_group, N_edge), with np.int8 elements. Since the permutation elements are signed, then they run from ||(-|E|||) to ||(+|E|||) (without 0), but np.uint8 is still sufficient for ||(|V| <= 127||).

The Pachner graph

Given the set of ||(G_i||), the Pachner graph ||({\cal P}||) is the graph obtained by using the 2-2 moves between the various ||(G_i||). The nodes of the Pachner graph are the graphs ||(G_i||), and the edges of ||({\cal P}||) are the valid 2-2 moves between the ||(G_i||). The remaining entries in the file pertain to the graph ||({\cal P}||). matrix_col, matrix_data, matrix_indptr: This is the information needed to construct the CSR adjacency matrix of shape (numGraph, numGraph) for the Pachner graph. This is stored in this manner so that the individual 2-2 moves are synchronized with the edges and permutations associated with the move, since some of the moves are multiple edges in the Pachner graph. Since matrix_col is giving the target graph labels, it is given as np.uint16, to accomodate the 227 graphs of ||(|V| = 18||); matrix_indptr gives the number of valid moves, so is set at np.int32 for the |V| = 18 case of XXX graph; matrix_data is only a series of 1's, and is chosen as np.uint8. move_edges: This records the edge label for the source edge of the 2-2 move as described in the source graph. This is an np.array of size (N_moves), with np.uint8 entries, since these edge labels are unsigned.The location of the moves for a given graph are given by indptr. move_perms: For every 2-2 move ||(G \to G'||), the permutation between the source and target graphs under the isomorphism is computed. This is a signed permutation of the edge labels, so the entries run from ||(-|E|||) to ||(+|E|||). This np.array has shape (N_moves, N_edges), with entries np.int8, since the signs are needed.

Example data file

Here we use the data for the ||(|V| = 12||) Pachner graph to demonstrate the specifics of this information.

console.text: Read in 17 graphs with V = 12 vertices

data.text/markdown: One thing we can investigate is the sizes of the various symmetry groups. We print these out now.

data.text/markdown: Notice that graphs 3 and 14 have a high degree of symmetry. This means that most of their edges are isomorphic under the automorphism group. Thus, these edges are treated as equivalent when computing the Pachner graph. In other words, if two edges are isomorphic, then a valid 2-2 move on one of these edges is not counted separately from a 2-2 move on the other. Thus, we expect that the graphs ||(G_3||) and ||(G_{14}||) have a low number of edges in the Pachner graph (i.e. a low number of 2-2 moves from them to other graphs). Conversely, there are other graphs with trivial automorphism groups (size 1). In these graphs, none of the edges are isomorphic, so a 2-2 move on any edge is considered distinct. If these moves do not eliminate the 3-connectedness of the resulting graph, they will appear as valid links in the Pachner graph. We can test this intuition by comparing the size of the graph symmetry groups to the number of links for each graph ||(G_i||) in the Pachner graph ||({\cal P}||). As we expect the graph of link number vs. group size follows a descending curve.

By testing different values of ||(|V|||), one sees that the number of symmetries tends to "pile up" at the lower end, as an increasing number of graphs have trivial automorphism groups for larger ||(|V|||). However, there is still a spread in the number of Pachner graph links, so the data points accumulate more on the left-hand side of the graph.
